company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but quality was low — the beat was driven by tariff refunds adding 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO benefit adding another 105 basis points. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% versus the expected +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Linearity improved through the quarter and management expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex as a stronger player in the fast-growing physical AI and robotics space.

MillerKnoll reported solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even without the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, delivering 42 cents on an adjusted basis. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the expected $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while the EPS band of $1.85–2.15 was left unchanged.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The leadership change is a routine executive transition with no financial guidance accompanying the announcement.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% against an expected 13.85%, despite revenue coming in slightly above estimates at $2.311 billion. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures weighing on consumer budgets and keeping retail soft, with rising material costs squeezing margins. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog year-over-year, though the company declined to provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing an impressive 22% weight loss outcome. The data reinforces Viking's position as a competitive player in the high-stakes obesity and metabolic disease drug market. This is a significant clinical catalyst that could drive meaningful upward revaluation of the stock.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is an earnings-focused note covering Tuesday September 22nd before the open, with no broad macro or Fed commentary included in today's release. Let's go through the key movers.

Starting with AutoZone — the company beat fourth fiscal quarter earnings at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the quality of that beat is questionable. The outperformance was largely driven by tariff refunds adding 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO benefit adding another 105 basis points. Underneath those one-time items, domestic comps missed badly — up only 1.6% versus the expected 3.1% — and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity through the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027, but this is a mixed print that's hard to get excited about.

Cognex is making a move in physical AI — the company is acquiring RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception, for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue with more than 50% year-over-year growth. This is a bullish strategic bet on the robotics and physical AI buildout.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid earnings beat — 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents — and importantly, they would have beaten even stripping out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind. That's a clean beat at 42 cents adjusted. Sales did miss, down 3.3% organically, but orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year revenue guidance was trimmed modestly while the earnings per share range was held unchanged. Mixed, but the earnings quality is actually decent here.

THOR Industries missed — 78 cents versus the expected 87 cents — with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year. Management's tone was cautious, flagging stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure squeezing consumer budgets. They won't give formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. On the positive side, dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost cuts are underway, and North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year. Still, this is a bearish print overall.

The biggest mover of the morning is Viking Therapeutics — shares are spiking pre-market after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss. That is a standout data point in the obesity drug race and puts Viking firmly on the map as a serious competitor in this space. Highly bullish.

Pentair named a new CFO, Bob Hau, effective November 1st — he brings prior experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Routine transition, nothing market-moving.

Bottom line for the session: Viking is the clear headline. AutoZone is a low-quality beat. THOR is a miss with cautious commentary. Watch how the market digests tariff-driven earnings quality across the board — it's a theme running through multiple prints this morning.
